neighbours.label: a perfect-tense verb of lasting impact on many people, setting up a count of those affected ('has helped [many]', 'has cost [countless]', 'have doomed')
fire: Over the years, this small clinic has helped thousands of patients in the valley.
Corruption has cost the country billions in lost investment.
Her cookbook has inspired a whole generation of home bakers.
Bad weather has ruined countless harvests in the region.
The free app has saved many students hours of revision time.
Online forums have helped me find some of my closest friends.
This simple trick has rescued plenty of failed sourdough loaves.
Poor coaching has doomed several promising players in the league.
quiet: Last Tuesday, a nurse at the small clinic helped one patient to the car.
The new roof cost my uncle about four thousand pounds.
Her cookbook sits on the shelf next to the kettle.
Bad weather delayed the harvest by a week in October.
The free app crashed on my phone during the exam.
An online forum told me where to buy the right screws.
This simple trick works best with a very hot oven.
Poor coaching was blamed after the team lost on Sunday.

notes: Top peaks: helped x6, cost, found, saved me, doomed, 'been in', mostly after has/have; output promotes many/countless/numerous. Near misses: same verbs in simple past with a single specific object.
